h1: JLC Technology Group Launches USDC Payments for Faster, Lower-Fee Checkout

headings.text: JLC Technology Group Launches USDC Payments for Faster, Lower-Fee Checkout
Faster and Lower-Cost Payments with USDC
Supporting a More Flexible Digital Manufacturing Experience

meta_description: JLCCNC now supports USDC payments for eligible CNC machining and sheet metal orders in the U.S., with lower transaction fees and 24/7 availability.
monitored_text: Home Newsroom JLC Technology Group Launches USDC Payments for Faster, Lower-Fee Checkout JLC Technology Group Launches USDC Payments for Faster, Lower-Fee Checkout Press Release Aug 27, 2026 Table of Contents Faster and Lower-Cost Payments with USDC USDC Payment Availability How to Pay with USDC USDC Payment FAQs Supporting a More Flexible Digital Manufacturing Experience About JLC Technology Group About JLCCNC We are thrilled to announce that JLC Technology Group now officially accepts stablecoin payments . US-based customers can now pay for JLCCNC, JLC3DP, JLCPCB, and JLCMC orders using USDC—enabling near-instant settlement, lower transaction fees, and 24/7 availability. Faster and Lower-Cost Payments with USDC Paying with stablecoins brings several tangible advantages directly to customers: Lower transaction costs – Customers only pay the blockchain network fee (Gas fee), which is typically a fraction of a dollar on networks like Solana or Polygon. There are no cross-border surcharges or hidden bank fees. No bank account or credit card required – Customers only need a crypto wallet, such as MetaMask or Coinbase Wallet. Fast and straightforward checkout – Customers can select stablecoin at checkout, connect their wallet, and confirm the transaction in just a few clicks, without entering lengthy card details or bank information. In short, USDC payments provide lower fees, instant processing, and a smoother checkout experience. USDC Payment Availability The current stablecoin payment setup includes the following conditions: Item Current Rule Supported business JLCPCB, JLC3DP, JLCCNC, and JLCMC Supported region United States only Supported stablecoin USDC only Supported networks Tempo, Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, Base Maximum per transaction Up to 10,000 USD Refund options Original wallet or JLC balance These rules reflect JLC's current stablecoin payment setup. Customers outside the United States will not see the USDC payment option at this stage. Any future expansion of supported regions will be announced separately. This launch supports USDC only . Other stablecoins, including USDP and USDG, are not currently supported. How to Pay with USDC Paying with stablecoins is simple and requires four steps. Step 1: Select Payment Method at Checkout On the JLC order confirmation page, select "Crypto (USDC)" . Step 2: Connect Your Crypto Wallet Customers will be redirected to a secure payment page, where they can connect using MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet , or any WalletConnect-compatible wallet. Step 3: Confirm and Sign the Transaction The payment page displays the amount due, denominated in USDC and pegged 1:1 to USD. Customers can confirm and sign the transaction in their wallet. Step 4: Payment Complete Once the transaction is confirmed on-chain, the order status will update automatically. Funds are settled in USD to JLC's account — JLC does not hold or manage any cryptocurrency. USDC Payment FAQs Q1: Which stablecoins are currently supported? USDC only. Other stablecoins, including USDT, USDP, and USDG, are not currently supported. Q2: Are there fees for stablecoin payments? Customers are responsible for the Gas fees (network transaction fees) of the chosen blockchain network. Fees vary by network — Solana, Polygon, and Base offer extremely low fees, often just a few cents. JLC Technology Group does not charge any additional fees for stablecoin payments. Q3: Is there a transaction limit? The per-transaction limit is 10,000 USD. Orders exceeding this amount are not eligible for stablecoin payment and require an alternative payment method. Q4: Are refunds supported? Yes. Refunds are processed back to the customer's original wallet or to the customer's JLC balance, subject to customer setup. Q5: Which regions are supported? Currently, stablecoin payments are available only for customers in the United States. Other countries are not supported at this time. Q6: How long does a stablecoin payment take to confirm? Confirmation time varies by network. Ethereum typically takes 3–15 minutes, while Solana, Polygon, and Base usually confirm within 5–30 seconds. During network congestion, times may be longer. Customers are recommended to use faster networks like Solana or Polygon for the quickest experience. Supporting a More Flexible Digital Manufacturing Experience The launch of USDC payments provides US-based customers with another way to complete orders across JLC Technology Group's digital manufacturing ecosystem. By supporting stablecoin payments, JLCCNC and other JLC platforms provide customers with a payment option designed around faster processing, lower transaction costs, and 24/7 availability. About JLC Technology Group Founded in 2006, JLC Technology Group provides integrated electronics and mechanical manufacturing services to more than 9.5 million customers across over 180 countries and regions. Its ecosystem includes EasyEDA for PCB design, JLCPCB for PCB fabrication and assembly, JLC3DP for additive manufacturing, JLCCNC for CNC machining and sheet metal fabrication, and JLCMC for mechanical components—enabling customers to move from prototype to production through a full-stack digital manufacturing platform. About JLCCNC JLCCNC is an online manufacturing platform providing professional CNC machining and sheet metal fabrication services for engineers, product developers, businesses, and makers worldwide. With a range of manufacturing capabilities and materials, JLCCNC helps customers accelerate prototyping and production with quality, speed, and affordability. As part of JLC Technology Group , JLCCNC provides customers with access to the group's integrated digital manufacturing ecosystem, including electronics manufacturing, 3D printing, and mechanical components.
